x: As we've already described, Marty had it covered. Running with that assurance that we have come to expect since we first met him last February, the lead went up ... and up ... and the Ian Logan memorial Bowl was ours to look after for another year.

Australian Marty Dent had a cracking run in the 3000 metres Steeplechase - first man home after the Kenyan clean sweep – and in his fifth Commonwealth Games Mick Jones went over 70 metres in the hammer to place 5th.
Marty Dent, fresh from his great run in the Commonwealth Games steeplechase, writes from Australia and sends congratulations on a fifth consecutive SEAA 12-Stage win.

“I ran into Marty at the end of the race – really nice guy – it was great to meet a fellow Belgravian in Kenya.” Marty Dent, running for Australia, had also benefited from a conservative start and placed, 71st and fifth scorer for his team.
Marty Dent, unlucky to have missed out on Olympic selection for Australia in 2008, won this year’s 16km City2Surf with a time of 41 minutes 12 seconds, the first Australian to win since 1997.
